title: The Loves of the Boy and Girl at School
logline: A schoolboy too shy to speak writes his love on a classmate's tablet; she answers, the teacher adds a verse, her master adds another, and the little tablet ends as a marriage contract.
moral: A sincere word, kindly received, can change a life; and the kindness of those in charge decides how the story ends.
tone: Warm romantic comedy told almost in mime: shy glances, three suspense beats that each resolve into kindness, one good joke on the teacher, and a quiet, tender ending.

beats.summary: A boy and a girl in one schoolroom.
He loves her and cannot say it.
He fears the classmates will notice.
While everyone is distracted he takes her tablet.
He writes two verses on it.
She reads and knows he means her.
She writes her answer beneath his.
The teacher walks in unnoticed and takes the tablet.
He remembers his youth and adds verses himself.
The girl's master arrives; the tablet lands in his hands.
He reads all three messages and understands.
He does not forbid the marriage and adds his blessing.
He teases the teacher as a bold matchmaker.
Judge and witnesses: married on the spot, then a feast.
Verses on a small tablet became the start of a shared life.
A long happy life; and nobody forgot the teacher's part.

The same room dressed for the wedding: u 0.5 (dusk in the window), lampsLit true plus two extra hangingLamp at x 250 and 750, mats replaced by a pale cloth 640 x 26 on the floor (x 180 to 820) carrying three foodTray, a string of small pennants across the back wall (red, white, yellow triangles, 9 of them).

The cottage door (anchor door) is the match-cut target for the tablet: scale the cottage if needed so its door is close to the tablet's 110 x 150 proportion.

props.description: The lawh, star of the film. At s 1: board 110 wide x 150 tall with rounded lower corners, brown frame 8 wide, cream writing face, and a top tab handle 40 x 26 with a hole r 6. The face has four horizontal bands, each 30 high. Each band carries two "verse" lines: every line is two wavy halves (hemistichs) with a gap, drawn as seeded squiggles with a few dots above and below so they read as Arabic handwriting without being text. Band inks: 1 blue (boy), 2 red (girl), 3 black (teacher), 4 green (master). Fields: x, y, s, rot, lesson 0..1 (four grey rows of separate letter-like marks), wipe 0..1, bands: [{fill 0..1, col, glow 0..1, medal: person pose or null}], face: front | back, glint. Returns pen (the current writing point) so a hand can follow it. Insert size s 4.6.
Planned prop (AN-098): reed pen 60 long and a small round inkpot 28 wide; ink colour parameter; one drop option.
Planned prop (AN-098, AN-113): round portrait of a person head, r 40 on the insert and r 9 on the hand-size tablet, used as each author's signature at the right end of a band. Eyes can gaze.
Planned small scroll with wavy lines (lines 0..3) and a red seal 0..1: the marriage contract, 160 wide when open.
Planned brass tray with bread, dates and a cup; three on the feast cloth.
Planned fat coin purse: the master's gift, with a folded yellow cloth (rectangle 90 x 30 with two fold lines) beside it.
Planned icon (AN-097): 70 x 110, with tip-over. Used once in S14.
Planned loose cushion 120 x 34, red with yellow dots: the teacher's seat, later the judge's.
Library heart, the film's only recurring symbol: over the boy, on the tablet, in the turban.

subtitles.ar: كان فتى حر وفتاة مستعبدة يتعلمان في مدرسة واحدة.|أحب الفتى زميلته حبًا شديدًا،|لكنه لم يعرف كيف يصرح بما يشعر به،|وكان يخشى أن يلاحظ بقية التلاميذ أمره.
subtitles.en: A freeborn boy and an enslaved girl studied in the same school.|He loved her deeply|but did not know how to tell her|without attracting his classmates’ attention.

subtitles.ar: في يوم انشغل الطلاب عن الفتى،|فأخذ لوح الفتاة الذي تكتب عليه دروسها.|وبدل الكلمات المعتادة، كتب بيتين|يسأل فيهما عمن أتعبه الحب ولم يعد يستطيع إخفاء ألمه.
subtitles.en: One day, while the other students were distracted,|he took her writing tablet|and wrote two verses|about a heart exhausted by secret love.

subtitles.ar: عادت الفتاة إلى لوحها، وقرأت الشعر فعرفت أنه يقصدها.|تأثرت حتى دمعت عيناها،|ثم كتبت تحته بيتين|تقول فيهما إنها لا ترد محبًا صادقًا يطلب قربها.
subtitles.en: She read the poem, understood he meant her,|and wept with feeling.|Beneath his words she wrote two verses|promising kindness to a sincere lover.

subtitles.ar: لم ينتبه الاثنان إلى أن المعلم دخل الفصل.|رأى اللوح وقرأ الرسالتين، لكنه لم يغضب.|تذكر أيام شبابه،|وكتب بدوره أبياتًا يشجع فيها الفتاة على مواساة الفتى.
subtitles.en: Neither noticed their teacher arrive.|He read both messages, but instead of becoming angry,|he remembered his youth|and added verses encouraging her to comfort the boy.

subtitles.ar: بعد قليل جاء صاحب الفتاة إلى المدرسة،|ووقع اللوح في يده.|وجد عليه شعر الفتى ثم جواب الفتاة ثم كلام المعلم.|قرأ الرسائل الثلاث، وفهم سر النظرات والدموع.
subtitles.en: Soon the girl’s owner came to school|and found the tablet.|He read the boy’s poem, her reply, and the teacher’s advice,|understanding their secret.

subtitles.ar: لم يمنع الرجل الزواج،|بل كتب سطرين يتمنى فيهما ألا يفترق الحبيبان.|ثم مازح المعلم بعبارة لاذعة،|قائلًا إنه لم ير من قبل معلمًا يعمل وسيطًا للحب بهذه الجرأة.
subtitles.en: He did not oppose their union.|He added a blessing that the lovers never part,|then jokingly rebuked the teacher|for acting as such a bold matchmaker.

subtitles.ar: استدعى الرجل قاضيًا وشهودًا إلى المدرسة،|وعقد زواج الفتى والفتاة في الحال. لم ينتظرا سنوات طويلة ولا رسائل أخرى.|وأقام صاحب الفتاة وليمة زفاف، وأكرم الزوجين إكرامًا كبيرًا.
subtitles.en: The owner summoned a judge and witnesses,|and the pair were married at once.|He arranged a wedding feast and treated the newlyweds generously.

subtitles.ar: تحولت الأبيات المكتوبة على لوح صغير إلى بداية حياة مشتركة.|عاش الفتى والفتاة معًا في سعادة،|كما تقول الحكاية، حتى فرّق بينهما الموت.|ولم ينس الناس أن المعلم شارك في قصتهما.
subtitles.en: Verses on a little writing tablet had led to marriage.|The pair lived happily together|until death, as the tale ends,|with their teacher part of the story.

new_assets.name: writingTablet
new_assets.description: School writing tablet (lawh) with a handle tab, four ink bands that write on, a lesson state, a wipe, band glow and author medallions; hand size and insert size from one function. Reusable for any school, scribe, letter, contract or message story.
new_assets.implementation: One function writingTablet(ctx, P). Board and frame with K shape paths and ink outlines; each verse half is a seeded polyline of 14 to 18 points (K.rng seeded by band and line) drawn with a dash offset so fill 0..1 reveals it from right to left; dots are small circles revealed when the stroke passes them. lesson is four rows of 7 separate short marks. wipe is a clip rectangle travelling right to left that fades lesson alpha behind it. glow is a halftone band in the ink colour under the lines. Return {pen: [x, y], bands: [{y0, y1, medalAt}]}.

new_assets.name: schoolRoom (palaceHall dressing: kuttab)
new_assets.description: School dressing for the merchant variant of palaceHall: mats, teacher cushion, book stand, inkpots, a shelf of spare tablets; and a feast dressing (cloth, trays, pennants, extra lamps). Reusable for any school, study circle or scribes' room.
new_assets.implementation: A function schoolDressing(ctx, {mats: [[x, y]], cushion, stand, shelf, feast}) drawn after palaceHall and before the cast; mats are rounded rectangles with weave lines and fringe, all baked once with bake(). Feast mode swaps mats for a cloth rectangle and adds pennants along a sagging line.

owner_questions: The girl's enslaved status is shown only by a plainer dress, bare feet and her standing with lowered eyes when her master enters; there is no chain, collar or label saying SLAVE (default: keep it this gentle).
The master is labelled HER MASTER on screen at 87.5 (default); the alternative is HER GUARDIAN, which is softer but less true to the script.
The boy and girl are drawn as teenagers (youth option), not small children, because the story ends in their marriage (default: teenagers; the classmates are smaller children).
A sparrow at the window and the teacher stepping out are added to show why "the pupils were distracted"; neither is in the script (default: keep both).
The verses on the tablet are drawn as handwriting-like squiggles, not real Arabic poetry, so nothing is written that the narrator does not say (default: squiggles).
The tablet flying out of the teacher's hands into the master's (89.1 to 92.2) is a comic reading of "the tablet fell into his hand" (default: keep the gag).
Death at 162.5 to 165.8 is shown as nightfall: the old couple fade from their bench and two stars appear; no bodies or graves (default: this gentle version).
Invented English lettering: THE BOY, THE GIRL, CHIRP!, GULP!, A LITTLE LATER..., HER MASTER, MATCHMAKER!, HA HA!, JUDGE, MARRIED!, SO SMALL!, THE END (default: all twelve).

SCRIPT: Arabic paragraph 7 has a sentence with no English counterpart ("they did not wait long years or more letters"); both texts are kept verbatim and P7 is split in three chunks so that the English never sits under the wrong Arabic.
SCRIPT: Arabic paragraph 2 says he wrote "instead of the usual words" and paragraph 6 says the master wrote "two lines"; the English omits both details. Kept verbatim; the picture follows the Arabic.
implementation_notes: Timeline: use timing.json word starts through w(p, n); every cue in this plan gives the Arabic word and its start time on the final MP3 (170.80 s). Film length 174.0 s (end_hold 3.2).
Set LIFE.t = t every frame so the whole class blinks; add hand blinks where a lid is set explicitly.
Build writingTablet first and test it alone at s 1 (band colours must still read at 110 x 150: at that size draw each band as two thick colour strokes, no dots) and at s 4.6.

Keep ONE insert framing (tablet 506 x 690 centred 500, 640) for S4, S6, S9 (from 92.8), S11 and S16 so the audience learns the four bands as a growing stack: blue 30.2 to 41.9, red 55.0 to 57.0, black 79.5, green 109.6 to 110.8.
Seated children: person {sit: 1, seat: floor}; the tablet rests on the knees (prop at local about [0, -70], rot 0.15) with handRW following the returned pen point while writing.
Back row is s 0.72 of the leads and drawn before them; give every member its own blink seed and stagger(i) delay; never move the three in unison.
Two lens looks only: the children at 71.0 (GULP!) and the teacher at 169.54.
Three suspense holds must be truly still (only pupils move): 15.6 to 16.5, 73.1 to 74.2, 105.46 to 107.46.
The LATER card at 84.9 to 85.3 hides the reset (camera key 0.01 s apart at the card midpoint): tablet moves to under the teacher's arm, pair one mat closer.

Flying tablet 90.48 to 92.18: x by kfn from the teacher's back (about 660) to the master's hands (about 300, 720), y a parabola peaking near y 360, rot three full turns easing out; all children gaze with lookAt at the prop.
Match-cut at 153.84: draw the yard with the cottage door at the exact panel rectangle the small tablet occupied on the previous frame; reveal wall and roof with a 0.4 s scale-out from the door.
Ageing at 160.56 to 163.2: person age 0 to 0.9 with kfn on both, the same costumes; sky u from 0.25 to 0.5; then alpha fade 163.72 to 164.9 while u goes to 0.72.
Sound: at most seven quiet effects, all in real gaps: pop 6.95, tick 20.5, whoosh 84.94, tick 105.15, chime 108.5, chime 170.75, thud 171.6. The narration has almost no pauses, so do not add more.
Lettering stays in the upper band of the panel (panel y 90 to 260) or beside figures, never over a face; labels at 28 px or more, MATCHMAKER! and MARRIED! at 44 px or more.
Subtitles: use the subtitles array as chunks_ar.txt and chunks_en.txt; P7 has three chunks on purpose.
warnings: The narration is dense: only three pauses of 0.6 s or more. Effects must stay sparse.
Up to ten figures share the room in S13 and S15; keep the back row small and baked where it does not move.
The person figure is front facing only: stage looks between the boy and girl with gaze and head tilt, and stage the window crowd with overlap rather than true back views.

youth, judge, quillInk, portraitMedallion, scroll, foodTray, purse, hourglass, floorCushion, flush, sneak, laugh, handOver, goldGlow are planned by other films and may not exist yet; fallbacks are given in new_assets.
Hand-size tablet bands are only 30 units high: colour, not detail, must carry the idea outside the inserts.
